posts.author: Kaveh
posts.content_md:
Hahaha. I had the exact same problem last time I did the exact same thing. Your eye is tricking you. The eye sees several colors, and assumes the average of the colors is somewhere in the mid green. So it assumes the 514 is higher wavelength than it actually is.

So the complex question arises - What is yellow? You have seen a part of why color science is so complex.

Same effect explains why you see things the same color no matter what the lighting conditions are, but of course they look different when you photograph them. 

But this one is so striking it has to be seen to be believed!!

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md: Also remember the eye modulates the colours in the scene on the photopic curve.

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md:
> **JohnFP:** I have read that article and found some of it's contents useful. I have a couple of other articles and have followed their formulas but still can't seem to get my replay swelled enough into the red.

i wasnt sure if you saw this one;

Red-- mix 3-30-250 using Potassium Dichromate spin on at 80-90 RPM, expose single beam 90-100 mj\cmE2 @ 514 if RH = 60% and T = 70 F. Process: develop 5 min., rinse, 30 sec in 1HAB @ 120 F and .86 SG. Dry with slow pull from LHAB followed by hot air. Color should be bright Red-Orange. 

Blue--Mix 9-30-250 using Ammonium Dichromate, spin on at 80-90 RPM, expose single beam 24 mj\cmE2 @ 458 if RH = 60% and T = 70 F. Process: develop 3 min., rinse, 15 sec in 1HAB @ 120 F and .86 SG. Dry with slow pull, color should be bright Blue to Blue-Green. 

This film was 2-4 hrs old, shorten times for older film. 

For 3 Color system use 10-30-250 and expose twice, once with 24 mj @ 458 and once with 50 mj @ 514. Then code the object for Red and use the same red procedure. 

heres the article

[/url][http://www.xmission.com/~ralcon/color.html](http://www.xmission.com/~ralcon/color.html)
